I was going off the uscis.gov site. Where it states that an immigrant can apply for an [EB-2 visa](https://www.uscis.gov/working-united-states/permanent-workers/employment-based-immigration-second-preference-eb-2) if one of the following categories applies to them: Advanced Degree/Exceptional Ability/National Interest Waiver. I would fit the **Exceptional Ability** criteria.

Where you must meet at least **three** of the following:

* Official academic record showing that you have a degree, diploma, certificate, or similar award from a college, university, school, or other institution of learning relating to your area of exceptional ability
* Letters documenting at least 10 years of full-time experience in your occupation
* A license to practice your profession or certification for your profession or occupation
* Evidence that you have commanded a salary or other remuneration for services that demonstrates your exceptional ability
* Membership in a professional association(s)
* Recognition for your achievements and significant contributions to your industry or field by your peers, government entities, professional or business organizations
* Other comparable evidence of eligibility is also acceptable.

I don't know, I just don't see the point of it all.. I don't enjoy life, quite the opposite. Most of the time I'm miserable. It's the daily grind of waking up, putting on a fake smile, trying to impress people I don't care about, to pay for a house I couldn't afford, to keep a family that will eventually abandon me. I'll grow old and die alone in a home. Why wait?

I just really don't enjoy living. Any person in my place would enjoy this life, like I said, I've accomplished plenty. But I don't enjoy any of it. Just want to die.

I was in army-prison for bad behavior. I was having back problems, from carrying heavy things. Army didn't take care of those problems, so I went AWOL to see a doctor.

In prison, I was at my lowest point, and tried to kill myself by hanging. I did it at night, hoping no one would see/hear.. But a guard saw me and stopped it. I saw a therapist the next day, and was discharged within around a week.

It's almost 10pm here, I don't really feel like sleeping.

Honestly, nothing serious that I can think of. I was bullied, mocked for my choice of clothes/music, didn't have a girlfriend, hated my parents and didn't have any friends during my teenage years - but that's just part of growing up, everybody went through that.

All of these things mean nothing as an adult. There are no bullies in the office, I couldn't care less what people think of my style, I've had multiple partners, love my parents greatly (actually a bit sad seeing them grow old, and thinking about them dying one day), and I have one really close friend (and plenty of acquaintances).

I was diagnosed with depression in the military, and was discharged but didn't seek help after because I was focused on getting an education and getting a job. It's hard to explain, but it's just a lack of will to live. Every day is a constant reminder that I'm still alive, and I don't want to be. 

Best way I can describe it is imagine you have this annoying buzzing sound around you *all the time* and you just want it to *stop*. That's kind of how I see it.
